In his president’s column for the Acoustical Society of America (ASA), Michael Vorländer recalls the 188th ASA meeting, held jointly with the 25th International Congress on Acoustics (ICA) in New Orleans. His muse is Louis “Satchmo” Armstrong (1901–1971), who overcame poverty and racism to become a world-famous musical innovator, and his song “What a Wonderful World.” Its technical hope, he writes, lives in acousticians’ work on climate monitoring and the social impact of noise; its social hope in the meeting’s warm, respectful atmosphere, where 30 young colleagues took part in the Early Career Acousticians Retreat.

The ICA was founded in 1951 as a subcommission of the International Union of Pure and Applied Physics (IUPAP), later became affiliated with IUTAM, and since 2006 has been a scientific member of the International Science Council; it took its present form under Larry Crum, who also chaired the 1998 ASA/ICA meeting in Seattle. Today it links 52 acoustical societies on every continent, plus eight international members such as I-INCE and the AES, and it launched the International Year of Sound 2020/2021, with the ASA as a leading sponsor.

The ASA itself has supported acoustics in developing countries since the 1990s, first through fellowships initiated by David Blackstock and now through its Committee on International Research and Education. Joint meetings continue: with the Acoustical Society of Japan in Honolulu on December 1–5, 2025, and with the European Acoustics Association in Brussels in spring 2027, home, he notes, of the world’s best chocolate.

Adapted into Chinese by Fanyu Meng from Michael Vorländer’s “From the President” column in Acoustics Today (2025). Read the original.
